summary: Publish honest corpus, coverage, and methodology transparency
description: Execution brief work unit 6/7. Destination: CallerSignal behaves like a trustworthy HIBP-style caller-campaign intelligence service: one search yields a calibrated answer, campaign history, concrete actions, private monitoring, verified organisation context, transparent corpus coverage, and an agent-native remote MCP surface.

intent_source.text: CallerSignal has a strong read-only lookup and risk presentation, but most results still expose numbering context rather than risk-capable campaign evidence, and the product lacks the recurring value loops, verified ownership workflows, public corpus transparency, and hosted agent access that make HIBP useful beyond a one-off search.

execution_brief.destination: CallerSignal behaves like a trustworthy HIBP-style caller-campaign intelligence service: one search yields a calibrated answer, campaign history, concrete actions, private monitoring, verified organisation context, transparent corpus coverage, and an agent-native remote MCP surface.
execution_brief.problem: CallerSignal has a strong read-only lookup and risk presentation, but most results still expose numbering context rather than risk-capable campaign evidence, and the product lacks the recurring value loops, verified ownership workflows, public corpus transparency, and hosted agent access that make HIBP useful beyond a one-off search.
execution_brief.chosen_approach: Make CallerSignal a HIBP-like caller-campaign intelligence service: model campaigns as the durable risk object; collect only structured first-party reports under privacy and moderation controls; add private watch notifications and verified organisation number portfolios; publish consumer campaign transparency and a hosted OAuth-aware MCP surface; keep source-rights, spoofing, no-safe-number, and no-lookup-popularity invariants.
non_goals: Scrape, copy, or derive reputation from unlicensed third-party caller-report databases.
Publish free-text accusations, requester identities, raw call histories, lookup trails, or real phone-number fixtures in Git.
Treat a displayed number, number ownership claim, lookup volume, or one unverified report as proof of caller identity, guilt, or safety.
Ship live outbound notifications, persistent personal data, or authentication against an undeclared provider or without explicit retention, deletion, abuse, and incident controls.
Turn the public consumer UI into an alternative source of truth distinct from CLI, MCP, and HTTP contracts.

source.recommendation: Make CallerSignal a HIBP-like caller-campaign intelligence service: model campaigns as the durable risk object; collect only structured first-party reports under privacy and moderation controls; add private watch notifications and verified organisation number portfolios; publish consumer campaign transparency and a hosted OAuth-aware MCP surface; keep source-rights, spoofing, no-safe-number, and no-lookup-popularity invariants.

requested_outcomes.text: Public metrics are derived only from enabled sources, eligible campaigns, verified portfolios, and privacy-thresholded aggregates; lookup volume never becomes reputation evidence.

Coverage explicitly names jurisdictions, risk-capable sources, freshness, last successful ingest, unavailable gaps, moderation thresholds, correction counts, and methodology version without vanity or unsupported totals.
The README and website make corpus limitations and the meaning of no matching evidence immediately understandable.
